facts.text: The CIUSSS de la Mauricie-et-du-Centre-du-Québec, the regional health authority based in Trois-Rivières, has a team of nearly 21,000 employees.
Kruger's Trois-Rivières mill employs more than 350 people and its Machine No. 7 produces 149,000 tonnes a year of newsprint, coloured construction paper and Krubook paper.
The Quebec government is providing $6,870,000 so researchers and entrepreneurs can use advanced energy-transition research facilities at UQTR in Trois-Rivières.
The Vallée de la transition énergétique innovation zone, designated in May 2023, spans Mauricie and Centre-du-Québec with UQTR, Bécancour, Shawinigan and Trois-Rivières as founding members.
Innovation et Développement économique Trois-Rivières is the single-window, first-line service the City mandates to support and coordinate economic development across its territory.

overview: Trois-Rivières had 139,163 residents in the 2021 Census, a 3.5 percent increase since 2016, which is steady rather than rapid growth. The city's 66,822 occupied private dwellings sit on 288.65 square kilometres along the St. Lawrence, halfway between Montreal and Quebec City, so most customers are within a short drive of the centre.

Health care, paper manufacturing and the university are the big employers, and the region has been designated an energy transition innovation zone. For a local business this means a stable, largely French-speaking customer base, a large public-sector payroll, and a growing cluster of research and clean-energy firms looking for suppliers.

byService.website-development: A website for Trois-Rivières should present clear French service pages and fast mobile performance, because a compact 288.65 square kilometre city means visitors often want directions and hours first.
byService.branding: Trois-Rivières branding benefits from linking a business to the city's manufacturing heritage and its new energy-transition identity, giving institutional and industrial buyers a reason to trust a local supplier.
